Independently recomputed all 30 c_t entries directly using ordered subset-pair enumeration; checked the six orbit partition and coefficient dominance.
correctness.rationale: For each ordered pair of four-subset embeddings A,B with |A∪B|=t, either their common positions demand incompatible pattern letters, giving zero, or their joint probability is 2^(−t). Counting valid ordered pairs on [t] produces the exact formula E[X_p²]=Σ_{t=4}^8 c_t(p)2^(−t) C(n,t) for every n≥4; mean C(n,4)/16 is immediate. Independent enumeration of all ordered four-subset pairs reproduced the thirty c_t entries for the six reversal/complement orbits: 0000=(1,20,90,140,70), 0001=(1,14,60,110,70), 0011=(1,12,56,104,70), 0010=(1,10,44,94,70), 0110=(1,10,42,84,70), 0101=(1,8,36,80,70). Adjacent rows are coefficientwise nonincreasing, with strictness at n≥6, only the 0010/0110 tie at n=5, and complete n=4 equality; degree-eight cancellation and c7 differences give leading n^7/645120 multipliers 70,40,34,24,14,10. The finite coefficient enumeration is exhaustive because t≤8; it proves the all-n theorem via the exact subset-pair identity.
residual_risks: The exact moment identity is a standard pattern-overlap technique, not claimed as novel in isolation.
Full distribution/tail stochastic dominance does not follow from variance order.

value.rationale: All sixteen length-four binary scattered patterns form a natural first moderately rich case of exact subsequence-count fluctuation comparison. The six-orbit hierarchy gives exact finite-n variances and a sharp universal strictness threshold, with constant-pattern fluctuations seven times alternating in the leading order despite equal means. An independently useful comparative statistic beyond a routine restatement of expectation.
residual_risks: Pattern length four is fixed; no claim for arbitrary pattern length or complete tail behavior.

limitations: Only uniformly random fair binary words and scattered length-four patterns; n≥4.
Generic hidden-word overlap methods and equality under reverse/complement are established prior work.
